subject: Alignment on latency SLOs vs dynamic throttles for EdgePilot trial
messages:
From: Sasha Moroz <sasha@clearpath.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot traffic profile + throttling concerns

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re finalizing go-live for the EdgePilot pilot (internal kickoff 10/11) and I wanted to flag one operational requirement up front: we expect a concentrated burst during the first 36 hours as clinicians and training cohorts hit the system. Our internal ops estimates are ~450 concurrent sessions with short completions (avg 60 tokens) and several scheduled bulk-import flows for historical intents.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood provide a temporary uplift to hosted burst allowances during the initial 36–48h so we don’t hit fairness-based throttles that would create high tail latency?
- We also need an explicit latency commitment during the pilot window (p95 and p99 targets) and a short note we can share with our SREs describing expected behavior when you fallback to fairness throttles.

I attached our pilot run plan for context. Happy to jump on a quick call if easier.

Best,
Sasha
Product Ops, ClearPath Health
[attachment: ClearPath_Pilot_RunPlan.pdf]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Moroz <sasha@clearpath.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot traffic profile + throttling concerns

Hi Sasha — thanks for the clear runbook. We can support a temporary uplift for the go-live window, but I want to set expectations and capture the guardrails so there are no surprises mid-run:

Summary proposal (short):
- Temporary burst uplift: hosted account will be allowed a 3x burst multiplier over baseline concurrent sessions for a 48-hour window starting on the go-live start time you confirm.
- Monitoring & rollback: We’ll enable enhanced token-level latency tracing and an alert to your SREs; if sustained degradation (p95 > 500ms for >15 minutes) we’ll automatically throttle back to baseline and notify both teams.
- Latency targets during uplift: target p95 < 350ms, p99 < 1.2s for typical text completions (subject to model size and prompt length).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Aditya — can you confirm the throughput cap we can guarantee in us-west for a 3x burst and any model/quantization caveats?
2) Karthik — we should prepare a brief SLA addendum + mutual action plan for signatures.
3) Sasha — if this summary looks good please confirm the exact 48h start window and attach any expected token size distribution.

I’ve looped Aditya and Karthik to scope the technical and legal bits. We’ll produce a one-page exception letter for your procurement team.

—Marissa
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sasha Moroz <sasha@clearpath.ai>
Date: 2026-10-03T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot traffic profile + throttling concerns

Thanks Marissa — quick technical note from the infra side:

What we can commit for the 48h uplift in us-west:
- Sustained throughput cap during uplift: ~1,200 completions/sec (cluster aggregate) assuming you use the curated small/medium models we demoed. That maps to the 3x concurrent-sessions uplift Sasha mentioned given your token profiles.
- Performance levers: enable prefix/KV caching and a token-batching window (50ms) to reduce per-token overhead. These are automatic on our hosted runtime but I’ll force conservative batching parameters for the pilot.
- Fallback behavior: when fairness policies engage we do a graceful token-shed (soft-throttling) where ongoing requests are allowed to finish but new requests receive a 429 backoff with Retry-After. We’ll also return an X-Redwood-Serving-Mode header so your app can surface the degraded mode.

I attached the stress test I ran against a similar profile last week — numbers show p95 ~280–330ms and p99 spike to ~1.1–1.4s under transient bursts; these are consistent with Marissa’s targets.

Action items for Sasha: please confirm peak TPS and typical prompt/token histogram so we can tune batching.

[attachment: stress-test-report.pdf]

—Aditya
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Sasha Moroz <sasha@clearpath.ai>
Date: 2026-10-03T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot traffic profile + throttling concerns

Sasha / team — a couple legal/ops notes:

1) For hosted customers we can produce a short SLA exception addendum that documents the temporary burst uplift, the monitoring commitments, and the rollback triggers. It won’t change our standard uptime SLA long-term, but it will give your procurement/legal teams a signed artifact for the pilot.

2) If you need lower tail latency guarantees (e.g., p99 hard cap), we can discuss a Dedicated or reserved routing path for the pilot, but that requires a short commercial commitment.

3) I’m attaching a mutual action plan template that we should complete together so responsibilities and communication channels are clear during the 48h window (escalation contact, on-call rotations, LOG_LEVELs for your SREs).

If Sasha confirms the start time I’ll draft the addendum and run it through our legal for signature.

[attachment: mutual_action_plan.xlsx]

—Karthik
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Sasha Moroz <sasha@clearpath.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T08:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot traffic profile + throttling concerns

Thanks — this all looks good and aligns with what we need. Confirming:
- We accept the 48-hour uplift starting 2026-10-11T02:00:00-07:00 (UTC-normalized start for our training cohort).
- We’ll share the token histogram and exact peak TPS by EOD 2026-10-05.
- For the procurement ask: please provide the written exception addendum and a DocuSign route so our procurement team can sign before the pilot start.

One follow-up question: can you explicitly call out the expected headers and error codes so our app can detect degraded mode and show the appropriate UI? Being able to present that behavior to clinical ops is important.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Sasha
Product Ops, ClearPath Health
